title: Late-night deploy handoff + quick runbook
content:
Context:
- Night shift roll of v0.9.3 → customer env (acme-finance-prod). Small change: kernel selection tweak + kv-cache TTL lowered to 10s.
- Went live 2025-02-18 22:40 PST behind canary (10% traffic). Smoke looked OK, will hand off to morning team with notes.

Quick summary for morning:
- What I did: pushed new runtime image redwood/runtime:v0.9.3-hotfix -> k8s cluster acme-prod (namespace: redwood-inference). Updated deployment redwood-inference-runtime, set env VAR KV_CACHE_TTL=10s.
- Why: memory footprint spiking for long-chat sessions; lowering TTL reduces KV pressure.
- Canary results: ~5% lat increase on 16k-seq tests but 12% reduction in GPU mem usage for heavy sessions. Baseline latency still within SLA for this customer (p99 < 300ms).

Immediate checklist (what to watch first thing):
1) Check error-rate rolling window (grafana: ACME_prod/infra/runtime/errors) — any spike > 0.5% for 30m -> rollback.
2) Check KV cache hit ratio (grafana: ACME_prod/runtime/kv_hit_ratio) — expected to drop ~6–8%.
3) Confirm model weights integrity on node-3 (sha256: 3a7f...c9) — see /opt/models/checksums.txt.
4) KMS logs: ensure no new KMS decrypt failures (cloud-kms logs) after midnight rotation.
5) Network: Confirm we did not hit firewall rule rate limits (edge-fw-acme-1). Look for tcp resets from 10.4.0.0/16 -> 35.200.10.0/24.

Commands I used (replayable):
- kubectl -n redwood-inference set image deploy/redwood-inference-runtime redwood-inference-runtime=redwood/runtime:v0.9.3-hotfix
- kubectl -n redwood-inference set env deploy/redwood-inference-runtime KV_CACHE_TTL=10s
- kubectl rollout status deploy/redwood-inference-runtime -w
- docker pull redwood/runtime:v0.9.3-hotfix && docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' redwood/runtime:v0.9.3-hotfix
- ssh acme-prod-node-3 'sha256sum /opt/models/llama-13b/weights.bin'  # expect 3a7f..c9

Known issues / anomalies observed:
- 23:05: intermittent GRPC retry loop from worker pool; trace points to grpc_client.go:142 where timeout is 4s. I bumped to 6s temporarily via env RPC_TIMEOUT=6s on canary pods.
- One node (node-5) reported OOM-kill for model loader process at 23:17; node-5 has older Nvidia driver (525.85). Ticketed: JIRA-PRIV-4123.
- KMS rotation warning at 23:45: service account acme-redwood-sa returned IAM_DENIED for decrypt on one request. Appears transient; retried successfully.

Roll-back plan (if morning sees regression):
- Step 1: Scale canary to 0 (kubectl scale deploy/redwood-inference-runtime --replicas=0 --namespace=redwood-inference-canary) then immediately scale baseline back to previous image redwood/runtime:v0.9.2-stable.
- Step 2: Revert KV_CACHE_TTL env var to 30s (kubectl set env ... KV_CACHE_TTL=30s).
- Step 3: Post-rollback: run synthetic load (scripts/loadtest/run_short.sh --profile=acme-smoke) and verify p99 latency and mem usage.

Open action items (to assign):
- @Mateo: driver audit on node-5 (confirm if we should push driver 535+). NOTE: acme only allows maintenance windows — coordinate with customer ops.
- @Infra: confirm firewall rule edge-fw-acme-1 did not change at 22:30–23:00 window.
- @SecOps: verify KMS key rotation audit for customer key acme-prod-kms-01, look for any denied entries.

Notes to morning on-call (Aisha -> morning-team):
- If you see repeated grpc retries from runtime, check RPC_TIMEOUT and Consumer-side backoff (linear->exponential). When in doubt, increase timeout in canary first before rollback.
- Model checksum location: /opt/models/checksums.txt (updated by preflight job). If checksum mismatch, do not restart service — escalate to Platform SRE.
- Look at node labels: node-5 has label legacy-driver=true. Filter: kubectl get nodes -L legacy-driver.

Loose thoughts / TODOs for follow-up doc: (not urgent)
- Add a small runbook snippet in Confluence for "KV_CACHE_TTL tuning" with measured mem/latency curves.
- Create an alert that correlates KV cache miss rate with GPU memory usage.
- Automation: add preflight that fails deploy if any node has legacy-driver=true and model weight > 10GB.

Random notes / scratch (may delete later):
- Customer contact: jen.huang@acme.com (ops lead) — pinged 22:55 that we started canary.
- Slack snippets: #cust-acme thread ts 167XXX shows customer load spike at 21:50 that likely increased baseline and triggered mem pressure.
- Morning reminder: keep the morning standup short — focus on metrics for deploy window 22:30–23:30.

End of handoff.
- Aisha
